verdict.reasoning: Patient states diarrhea for past three days and going to the toilet 'around, five to six times a day' with 'definitely watery, loose stools.'
Patient: 'it started with vomiting, so I vomited a couple of times. Uh, but then, that went away.' This supports onset with a few vomiting episodes that have resolved.
Doctor asks about blood in stools; patient replies: 'No, not that I could see.'
Doctor: 'have you noticed any other symptoms, like tummy pain?' Patient: 'Uh, not, not really, no.'
Patient: 'I feel like I don't drink enough... I feel dehydrated again' and earlier 'I feel very dehydrated.'
Patient: 'have you managed to eat anything, solids?' – 'Uh, not much, not much. So just a little bit, but... I don't really feel like, uh, I have appetite.'
Patient: 'probably at, at the beginning I was feeling I had a bit of temperature, but now I feel, I feel kind of fine.' This implies initial feverish feeling now resolved.
Patient: 'I feel very weak though.'
Doctor: 'Any headaches or muscle pains?' Patient: 'Not, not really, no.' This supports no headache or myalgias.

No suspect food: Doctor asks about 'takeaway food, or any dodgy restaurant food?' Patient: 'Uh, not that I remember, no.' No sick contacts: Doctor: 'Have you been around anyone unwell, with diarrhea...?' Patient: 'Hmm, not that I know.'
Patient: 'I do suffer of asthma.'

Patient: 'So, I do have my inhalers... I use infrequently, let's say only when I have...' Doctor clarifies 'Is that the blue inhaler?'; patient confirms 'Yes it is.' This supports PRN blue inhaler use.
Doctor: 'Do you have any allergies to medications?' Patient: 'Um, not that I know of.'
Patient: 'my father has, high uh, well used to have high blood pressure. He actually... died, of, bowel cancer.'
Patient re mother: 'she has diabetes.' Doctor: 'Do you know if that's type one or type two?' Patient: 'Uh, it's type two.'
Living situation: Doctor: 'Who lives at home with you?' Patient: 'Ohh I, I live alone.' Job: Doctor: 'What do you do for work?' Patient: 'I'm a software engineer.'
Doctor: 'Have you taken time off work recently?' Patient: 'Uh, yes, yes I have... These last three days I've been feeling, really unwell, so I couldn't work.'
Doctor: 'regarding your smoking and alcohol. Do you do either of those?' Patient: 'not really, I drink infrequently, like socially let's say, and I don't smoke.'

Doctor diagnoses 'gastroenteritis... a tummy bug... an infection of your tummy... normally lasts about three to five days.' Dehydration risk is implied by symptoms but not stated; 'likely self-limited viral' is not mentioned explicitly.

Doctor: 'you can drink plenty of fluids... You can get things from the pharmacy, which is called Dioralyte... a type of fluid replacement drink.' This aligns with clear fluids and oral rehydration solution.
Doctor: 'you can take some Paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak.' Also advises rest implicitly by recommending time off work.
Specific dietary advice to 'avoid dairy, caffeine, and alcohol' and 'small frequent sips then bland foods' is not discussed in the transcript.

Doctor: 'I would probably advise you to continue taking time off work for next day or two... normally you have to be diarrhea-free for about twenty four to forty eight hours, before you return back to work.'
Detailed return precautions (5–7 days, high fever, worsening weakness, signs of dehydration, bloody stools, severe abdominal pain, inability to keep fluids) are not enumerated in the transcript.
Doctor: 'Let's see how the next few days go. And if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me.'
